claims.statement: KNF states that account-information service in Poland is regulated activity requiring registration even though it does not require a full authorization decision; a registered AISP also has insurance or equivalent security, reporting and supervision-cost obligations.

PSD2 limits an AISP to explicit user consent, designated payment accounts and associated transactions, and forbids access, use or storage for purposes beyond the account-information service explicitly requested by the user.

EDPB guidance says financial-transaction analysis can reveal or infer special-category personal data, that a DPIA will most probably be required, and that explicit consent may be the applicable Article 9 derogation when substantial-public-interest law does not apply.

The 2024 KCPU study found that 31.7% of respondents aged 15+ had gambled for money in the prior year; among gamblers, 8.2% were low risk, 4.2% moderate risk and 1.6% high risk under the report's original CPGI threshold, demonstrating a real harm population but not B2B willingness to pay.

Direct incumbent documentation shows that Revolut already offers Polish users an instant gambling block with a 48-hour removal delay, Kontomatik already assigns a gambling transaction label in Poland, and Monzo reported more than 400,000 users had activated its gambling block by January 2022.

Hypothesis: an institutional distributor will pay for consented longitudinal guardrails and user-controlled support export beyond native blocking and generic categorization; no paid pilot, buyer commitment, conversion, retention or outcome evidence was found.

contrary_evidence: Revolut already gives Polish customers a no-extra-charge gambling block, so a bank can treat basic self-exclusion as a native account feature rather than a paid third-party product.
Kontomatik already exposes a gambling label for Polish transaction data, making merchant categorization available from an established local open-banking supplier.
Monzo's large activation count supports user interest in blocks but also shows that banks can build and distribute the feature themselves.
EDPB guidance indicates that transaction profiling has a considerable chance of processing special-category data, materially increasing consent, DPIA and security burdens.
The KCPU study shows that most gamblers are classified as safe and does not establish that institutions will pay for monitoring or that transaction alerts improve outcomes.

economics.acquisition_route: Build only with synthetic or volunteered test data, complete a counsel-reviewed data map and DPIA plan, then seek one paid design partnership with a financial-wellbeing or support provider. Use an existing registered AISP and enrichment vendor before considering own registration.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Unvalidated scenario, not a forecast: 150,000 opted-in monthly active users at PLN 4 monthly B2B revenue would equal PLN 7.2m annual recurring revenue; at 30% operating profit and a 4x value, a 70% founder stake would be about PLN 6m. A 5-8 year route requires trusted distribution, demonstrated benefit, low incident rates and durable contracts; user count, price, margin, valuation and timing are not evidenced.
economics.founder_time: 12-18 hours per week for synthetic-data product work, compliance design and one enterprise integration; qualified partners must own clinical care, crisis response and regulated AISP operations unless the business later staffs them.
economics.gross_margin_basis: Unvalidated planning range: 65-80% after AISP or enrichment fees, cloud and security controls, support, insurance and ongoing compliance. Enterprise integration, DPIA work, penetration testing and incident readiness may make early deployments materially more service-heavy.
economics.payback: Unvalidated target: 12-24 months after one enterprise minimum or roughly 15,000-30,000 paid active users; recalculate after a written AISP quote, security scope, paid pilot price and measured support burden.
economics.pricing: Unvalidated planning hypothesis: PLN 15,000-50,000 monthly platform minimum per large distributor or PLN 2-6 per opted-in monthly active user, with no user charge where possible. No public source establishes Polish institutional willingness to pay at these levels.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Institutional contracts may recur annually and opted-in users may monitor continuously, but easy consent withdrawal, remission and deletion are product requirements. No renewal or active-use evidence exists.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: embedded distribution, auditable consent UX, user-corrected labels and ethically measured intervention outcomes improve the workflow while raw account data remains purpose-limited and non-transferable
fingerprint.customer: financial-wellbeing apps, banks, employee-assistance programs and debt-support organizations serving adults who voluntarily seek gambling-spend visibility
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: embed through regulated fintech, bank and support organizations rather than acquire vulnerable consumers with paid social ads; begin with synthetic data and a compliance-reviewed prototype
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: consent and data-minimization interface, account-feed connection through a regulated provider, gambling-pattern classification, user-set alerts, guardrail tracking and user-controlled support export sold as B2B software
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: the institutional distributor pays a platform minimum and per-consenting-active-user fee; no fee is earned from gambling operators or adverse decisions about the user
fingerprint.problem_trigger: a user notices loss of control, a support journey begins, or a financial-wellbeing provider needs a private opt-in monitoring feature

founder_fit: The work combines data science, finance and first-hand understanding of betting behavior without requiring public disclosure or an influencer persona.
A synthetic-data prototype and narrow B2B design partnership fit the founder's preference for measurable, low-capital validation.
Privacy engineering, enterprise procurement and regulated-partner management add specialist work beyond model development and require counsel and security support.
The founder must keep the product in voluntary self-control and support workflows rather than clinical diagnosis or adverse decisioning.
risks: Financial transactions can reveal or allow inference of special-category personal data; an invalid consent basis, excessive purpose or security incident could cause serious user harm and regulatory exposure.
AISP access is regulated, purpose-limited and accompanied by insurance, reporting and security duties; a partner contract does not remove the need to map each party's GDPR role and permitted purpose.
Merchant labels can miss transfers, cash withdrawals, payment intermediaries or newly named merchants, while false positives can stigmatize or distress users.

Revolut already offers a gambling block to Polish customers, Monzo and Starling offer similar controls, and Kontomatik already labels gambling transactions in Poland, so categorization and simple alerts are weak differentiation.
Banks may prefer to build a free native control, buy enrichment from an established vendor or avoid the reputational and support burden altogether.
Enterprise security reviews, procurement and compliance cycles may exceed the founder's part-time availability before revenue.

structure.control_point: long-term white-label distribution integrations plus a purpose-limited, user-authorized consent, feedback and outcome workflow
structure.critical_dependency: a compliant AISP route, valid GDPR and any Article 9 explicit consent, sufficiently accurate classification, secure processing and evidence that users benefit and institutional buyers will pay for a non-adverse-use feature

thesis: Offer banks, fintech wellbeing tools, employee-assistance providers and debt-support services a white-label feature through which an adult explicitly opts in to classify gambling-related account transactions, set personal guardrails, receive private alerts and export a self-chosen support summary. Use a registered AISP route, map the exact purpose and controller roles, obtain GDPR and any Article 9 explicit consent required for inferred health-related patterns, minimize retention and prohibit underwriting, employment, insurance, gambling marketing or other adverse use. Because Polish open-banking vendors and banks already expose gambling labels or blocks, the controllable asset must be embedded distribution, auditable consent and evidence that the voluntary intervention helps users—not raw transaction categorization.
title: Opt-In Betting-Spend Safety API
uncertainties: Which Polish bank, fintech, employee-assistance or debt-support buyer owns budget for a voluntary feature that cannot support underwriting or other adverse decisions?
Does the precise workflow process inferred health data under Article 9 GDPR, and what explicit-consent and DPIA design will regulators and partners accept?
Can a partner AISP and enrichment contract permit continuous monitoring, feedback, alerting, deletion and the exact retention schedule?
What recall, precision and error distribution are achievable across card payments, bank transfers, cash and intermediated deposits in Poland?
Which user outcome can be measured ethically without claiming diagnosis or treatment, and does the feature produce incremental benefit beyond native gambling blocks?
What are real AISP, enrichment, insurance, penetration-test, hosting, integration and customer-support costs?
Will users maintain consent and active monitoring long enough to create value without feeling surveilled?
